title: The Merchant's Turban and the Camel (ES)
summary: An arrogant merchant wears an impossibly tall turban to impress the court. A passing camel provides an unforgettable lesson in modesty.
full_text:
A fabulously wealthy spice merchant named Seth Makhanlal arrived in Agra from Gujarat. Swollen with vanity, he had a royal turban maker construct a towering turban made of thirty yards of gold-brocaded silk, adorned with emerald brooches and a peacock feather, rising nearly three feet above his head!

Strutting through the streets of Agra, the merchant looked down his nose at ordinary citizens, demanding that everyone clear the way for his magnificent headdress.

He arrived at the palace gates to petition Emperor Akbar for a royal trade monopoly.

As Makhanlal stepped proudly through the royal courtyard, a camel train carrying sacks of royal fruit was passing through the gate. One of the camels, seeing the green peacock feather and the dangling gold fringe on the merchant's towering turban, mistook it for a bundle of fresh mountain sugarcane!

The camel leaned its long neck down, grabbed the turban in its giant yellow teeth, and yanked!

*Whoosh!*

The entire thirty yards of silk unraveled like a spinning spool! The turban was lifted off the merchant's head, revealing his shiny, completely bald skull to the entire assembly of guards, courtiers, and foreign ambassadors!

The camel munched on the peacock feather, while thirty yards of gold silk trailed through the horse manure on the pavement.

Makhanlal covered his bald head with his hands, shrieking in humiliation, while the courtyard erupted in deafening laughter!

Emperor Akbar and Birbal watched the spectacle from the balcony.

Birbal smiled with gentle irony:

'You see, Your Majesty? When a man builds his dignity upon outward height and flashy silk, a passing camel can strip away his entire glory in a single second!

'If Makhanlal had worn the humble turban of a modest merchant, he would still possess his dignity. But pride always erects a towering monument so that its fall may be witnessed by the entire city!'

Akbar laughed heartily, and Makhanlal wrapped a simple cotton cloth around his head, cured forever of his foolish vanity.
